proposals.before: The crowner knelt and set the cup east of the offering mat, rose, and stood south-facing west of the seat.

proposals.reason: In capping ritual, 冠者 is the person who has just been capped (the prince), not the guest who crowns; the idiomatic also omits 升筵.

proposals.before: The crowner ascended the mat, knelt and set the cup east of the offering mat, rose, and stood west of the mat facing south.
proposals.after: The one who was capped ascended the mat, knelt and set the cup east of the offering mat, rose, and stood west of the mat facing south.
proposals.reason: 冠者 here means the newly capped prince continuing the wine rite, not a crowner.

proposals.before: The cap-assistant knelt and removed the advancement-worthy cap; the guest stepped down three ranks, took the coronet, and crowned him.
proposals.after: The guest's cap-assistant knelt and removed the advancement-worthy cap; the guest stepped down three ranks, took the coronet, and crowned him.
proposals.reason: Chinese specifies 賓之贊冠者; the idiomatic drops the guest attribution present in the source and literal.

proposals.before: The prince rose; the guest bowed to the prince to go to the inner room; dressed in dragon robes and came out square west of the inner room door facing south.
proposals.after: The prince rose; the guest bowed to the prince to go to the inner room; he dressed in dragon robes and came out west of the inner room door facing south.
proposals.reason: 方 here is not 'square'; parallel units have 出房戶西, and the literal lacks a subject for the dressing clause.

proposals.before: When the guest left, the prince received him east-facing; kinsmen bowed; the prince returned the bow.
proposals.after: When the guest left, the prince appeared east-facing; the kinsmen bowed to him; the prince returned the bow.
proposals.reason: 皇子東面見 with 諸親拜之 means the prince presented himself east-facing for kinsmen's bows, not that he received the departing guest.

proposals.before: At first, when the guest departed, the prince received him facing east; kinsmen bowed to him; the prince returned the bow.
proposals.after: At first, when the guest departed, the prince appeared facing east; the kinsmen bowed to him; the prince returned the bow.
proposals.reason: 見 here is the prince appearing for the kinsmen's salute after the guest's departure, not receiving the guest.

proposals.before: The guest filled the courtyard, bowed east, and left; grooms followed; followers received the horses with obeisance outside the gate.
proposals.after: The guest, facing the courtyard gifts, bowed east and left; grooms followed; followers received the horses with obeisance outside the gate.
proposals.reason: 賓當庭實 means the guest takes position facing the courtyard offerings (庭實), not that he filled the courtyard.

proposals.before: The guest filled the courtyard, bowed east, departed; horse-leaders followed out; followers received the horses with obeisance outside the gate.
proposals.after: The guest, facing the courtyard gifts, bowed east and departed; horse-leaders followed out; followers received the horses with obeisance outside the gate.
proposals.reason: 當庭實 is positional relative to the courtyard gifts, not 'filled the courtyard'.

proposals.reason: 驚冕 is the Tang ritual 鷩冕 (pheasant coronet) grade; translating as 'startled' misreads the official dress term.
